0.0.n: Points to the person being described, rather than an object.

0.1.n: A formal word for a person, giving the narration a somewhat old-fashioned tone.

0.3.n: Japanese leaves whose mother unstated; the context supplies her.

0.4.n: Marks the mother as the other person in the relationship.

0.5.n: Links 母親と to 相性: compatibility with her mother.

0.6.n: Describes how well two people get along.

0.7.n: Describes their relationship in strongly negative terms.

0.8.n: だっ is the form of だ used before the past ending た.

0.9.n: Completes だった, placing the poor compatibility in the past.

0.10.n: Introduces the reason for her move in the following line.

1.0.n: Suggests having only herself to rely on, without possessions or support.

1.1.n: Marks the circumstances in which she sets out to live.

1.2.n: The て-form of 生きる connects to いく, expressing living on into the future.

1.3.n: An old-fashioned form of いく expressing resolve here, not the negative meaning won't go.

1.4.n: Marks 生きていかん as her resolve or purpose for moving.

1.5.n: A noun used with する for going to the capital, here Tokyo.

1.6.n: A classical form of する expressing a completed action, giving the narration an antique flavor.

2.2.n: Begins the emphatic expression それはそれは, rather than pointing to a specific thing.

2.3.n: Pairs with the first それ in a repeated expression that intensifies the description.

2.4.n: Repeats それ as part of それはそれは, building extra emphasis.

2.5.n: Completes それはそれは, which emphasizes just how diligently she worked.

2.6.n: Repeating this word underscores her sustained effort.

2.7.n: A casual shortening of アルバイト, used with する to mean working a part-time job.

2.8.n: The connecting form of する links her part-time work to what follows.

3.0.n: Refers to everyday costs such as food and housing.

3.1.n: Joins the two types of expenses she earns money to cover.

3.3.n: Marks living and school expenses as the money she earns.

3.4.n: The connecting form of 稼ぐ links earning money to supporting herself.

3.7.n: Used in 生計を立てる, the standard expression for supporting oneself financially.

3.8.n: Marks 生計 as the object of 立てる in this fixed expression.

3.9.n: A form of 立てる; together with 生計を, it means earning a living.

3.10.n: A form of the classical completion ending ぬ, not the usual particle に.

3.11.n: A classical ending that presents the event as past, lending a storytelling tone.

4.0.n: Names the setting where her abilities and qualities stand out.

4.1.n: Marks school as the setting for the description.

4.2.n: Adds a topic frame to で, shifting attention to her life at school.

4.3.n: Emphasizes that the following descriptions fit her perfectly.

4.4.n: A four-character expression describing someone who possesses both intellectual ability and physical beauty.

4.6.n: Literally combines scholarly and martial pursuits; in a school setting, it usually describes academic and athletic excellence.

5.0.n: Combines with の to describe students besides her.

5.1.n: Connects 他 to 生徒, forming other students.

5.2.n: Refers to her fellow pupils at school.

5.3.n: Makes the group of students explicit.

5.4.n: Highlights that her fellow students, too, admire her.

5.5.n: Describes looking up to someone; the clause directly modifies 優等生.

5.6.n: Describes a student with excellent performance, often implying good behavior too.

0.lit: This person, because compatibility with her mother was the worst,
0.tip: ため follows a reason and means because here.

1.lit: With herself alone, intending to go on living, she moved to Tokyo.
1.tip: いかんと expresses an old-fashioned resolve to live on, not a refusal to go.

2.lit: Diligently, so very, very diligently, she worked part-time,
2.tip: それはそれは is a repeated expression that strongly intensifies the description that follows.

3.lit: Earning living expenses and school expenses, she somehow established a livelihood.
3.tip: 立てにけり uses classical endings to give an ordinary account of making a living an old-fashioned storytelling flavor.

4.lit: At school, truly possessing talent and beauty, accomplished in both scholarly and martial pursuits.
4.tip: These two four-character expressions praise her beauty, intelligence, and academic and athletic abilities.

5.lit: A model student whom other students also admire.
5.tip: 他の生徒たちも憧れる comes before 優等生 and describes the student, without needing an English-style whom.
